+## 10. Text Kernels And Lazy Sequences
+
+The [chapter 19 string contract](../../../etas/docs/design/19-standard-library.md#1-strings-and-text-apis)
+and [std architecture](../../../etas-frontend/docs/architect/etas-std-design.md#65-stdtext)
+define the complete API inventory. Reuse `etas_builtin`, `etas_std`,
+`etas_core` and engine adapters; do not create text/Unicode/iterator crates or
+add new dependencies as part of this architecture update.
+
+### 10.1 Kernel Ownership
+
+Extend the existing `text/` domain by function, as shown in section 4:
+
+| File / subdomain | Responsibility |
+|---|---|
+| `query.rs` | Byte length/emptiness, scalar count, ASCII queries; no numeric parsing |
+| `search.rs` | Exact matching, forward/reverse search, shared finite empty-pattern progression |
+| `split.rs` | Eager/lazy splitting and line/whitespace segmentation using shared scanners |
+| `bounds.rs`, `slice.rs` | Checked position conversion and normalized interval/boundary validation; byte/scalar coordinates stay distinct |
+| `transform.rs` | Locale-independent case/trim/replace primitives; no eager conversion of every sequence output |
+| `join.rs`, `string.rs` | Borrowed sizing/bulk assembly and explicitly bounded primitive string operations; preserve existing unique-buffer optimizations |
+| `parse.rs` | Complete numeric/bool token parsing, concrete width/range checks and stable rendering |
+| `format.rs` | Bounded template scanning/substitution primitive used by the ordinary std implementation |
+| `char.rs` | Scalar properties, ASCII digit and scalar/u32 conversion |
+| `iteration/` | Engine-neutral sequence recipe, cursor state and incremental step semantics |
+| `unicode/` | Pinned segmentation/normalization/full casefold behavior and versioned data |
+| Existing `codec/text.rs` | UTF-8 bytes/text conversion and explicit malformed-input policy |
+
+Move the existing `TextQuery::ParseI32` logic into `parse.rs`; it must no longer
+emit a host-language error string as the source `TextError`. Replace the old
+`TextTransform::Lines -> TextOutput::Array` contract with a lazy sequence
+recipe. `split` remains eager, while `split_iter` uses the same scanner lazily.
+Do not leave competing authoritative implementations in these old branches.
+
+Ordinary std algorithms remain Etas flows where expressible. Kernels provide
+storage/scanning/Unicode primitives and explicit optimizations, not a private
+host operation for every public API. A kernel replacement of an ordinary std
+flow must preserve its checked return/effect contract and edge cases.
+
+### 10.2 Shared Cursor Contract
+
+Use neutral Rust data inside this crate, conceptually:
+
+```rust
+pub enum TextSequenceKind {
+    Chars,
+    CharIndices,
+    Lines,
+    Split,
+    Whitespace,
+    Matches,
+    Graphemes,
+    GraphemeIndices,
+}
+
+pub enum TextElement {
+    Scalar(char),
+    IndexedScalar { byte: usize, scalar: char },
+    Segment { start: usize, end: usize },
+    IndexedSegment { byte: usize, start: usize, end: usize },
+    Match { start: usize, end: usize },
+}
+```
+
+`TextSequencePlan` carries the operation and immutable configuration, such as
+the separator, not an engine value or native iterator pointer.
+`TextCursorState` records the next byte position, terminal/empty-match phase
+and operation-specific scanner state. Its state is operation-tagged, validated
+against the plan and source, and cannot be an arbitrary unchecked byte offset.
+`step(source: &str, plan, cursor, control)` yields one `TextElement`, end, or
+an explicit continue-at-safe-point result. It never materializes all elements.
+
+The engine retains immutable source/configuration ownership and owns a separate
+cursor per loop. The kernel borrows source only for one bounded step, returning
+ranges/scalars rather than storing a self-referential `std::str` iterator.
+Constructing/copying a sequence does not scan/copy the whole source or share a
+mutable cursor. Sequential traversal advances from saved state, not repeated
+`chars().nth(n)` or a prefix rescan per element. Empty-pattern state must allow
+the final empty match exactly once and then terminate.
+
+No HIR, AIR, frame, closure, Host service, checkpoint writer or cancellation
+source is stored here. Long scanners/transformations receive a narrow engine
+work-control interface for byte/node/output accounting and safe-point polling;
+the engine still owns limits, cancellation, scheduling and terminal arbitration.
+If a single element spans a large input, incremental scanner state permits
+yield/cancel without publishing a partial element. Iteration purity does not
+make it exempt from execution limits.
+
+### 10.3 Bounds And Typed Outcomes
+
+Reuse the existing checked integer/Index conversion and collection interval
+rules; text adds byte/scalar/grapheme boundary interpretation. Compare wide
+integer bounds before conversion to `usize`, normalize endpoints with checked
+arithmetic, and validate before slicing. Rust indexing panics, wrapping casts,
+clamping and lossy UTF-8 repair are not source semantics.
+
+`TextFailure` is a structured kernel outcome mapping one-to-one to the seven
+`std.text.TextError` variants. Preserve the difference between:
+
+- a successful absent match/optional access: `None`;
+- a checked slice/index/search-start failure: raised `Error<TextError>`;
+- a parser/formatter rejection: `Result::Err(TextError)`;
+- resource exhaustion, cancellation, invalid checked ABI or allocation failure:
+  the existing execution/adapter failure channel, not a fabricated TextError.
+
+The ABI adapter resolves the expected std enum/variant identity through checked
+type information. A Rust display string, arbitrary record or same-named user
+enum is not a substitute. An existing carrier using a variant tag must validate
+that tag against this expected identity before constructing an Etas value.
+`InvalidIndex`, `InvalidRange`, `NotCharBoundary` and `LengthOverflow` follow
+chapter 19's distinctions. `TextCodecError` remains separate.
+
+Search is exact UTF-8 content matching. Share its non-overlapping and finite
+empty-pattern rule with split/count/replace. Numeric parsing consumes all input,
+does not trim, uses the declared concrete numeric width and distinguishes syntax
+failure from representability overflow. Formatting supports only numeric
+placeholders/escaped braces and already-rendered strings; there are no implicit
+callbacks, reflection or interpolation evaluation.
+
+### 10.4 Unicode And Resource Contracts
+
+Unicode scalar properties, whitespace, case conversion, full casefold,
+normalization and extended grapheme segmentation must use a coherent pinned
+data release. Keep its data/algorithm fingerprint in `unicode/version.rs` and
+publish it through std compatibility metadata. Reuse existing implementation
+components only if their supported version and behavior match that contract;
+the presence of ICU transitively elsewhere is not an implementation proof.
+Missing coverage uses release-pinned data/algorithms within this existing
+module, with provenance and conformance tests, not a new crate, runtime download
+or OS locale backend. Toolchain Unicode helpers require the same version check.
+
+Normalization forms are selected by the checked `Normalization` enum, not an
+unvalidated string. Full casefold is not lowercase; grapheme reverse is not
+scalar reverse. Do not normalize ordinary equality/search or translate offsets
+from transformed text back to the input silently.
+
+`len` and emptiness are constant-time; scans and ordinal conversion may be
+linear. Reuse/extend `join_projected` for checked total-size calculation plus
+bulk assembly, without cloning a temporary parts array or repeatedly copying
+an accumulated prefix. `repeat` checks multiplication and fast-paths empty
+input/zero count; an arithmetic overflow is `LengthOverflow`, not allocation
+failure. Padding width counts scalars. All allocating/scanning operations honor
+active limits before growth and during work, not after a full allocation.
+
+Tests cover every API family, all integer/float widths, Unicode conformance
+vectors, malformed/large inputs, exact errors, empty patterns, line endings,
+range bounds, cursor independence/progress and input/output allocation scaling.
+Use the same pure vectors with interpreter and future AIR adapters; test actual
+bytes/counters/allocations rather than only wall-clock thresholds. Source-level
+fixtures remain in the existing downstream test crates.

+## 9.6 Compiler Service

+network/filesystem/memory, with protocol/{request,response,error}.rs,
+service/client.rs, validation/identity.rs and limits/accounting.rs.

+revision-bound installation evidence before returning A/F. Compile rejection raises
+Error<CompileError>(kind=rejected); operational failure of either service uses
+kind=service. Authority denial, cancellation and limit exhaustion retain their
+own enforcement semantics rather than being disguised as reparable source errors.

+cache misses/retries/revisions do not reset parent budgets. Configure CPU/memory
+ceilings using durations/bytes and verify actual work/allocation/cleanup bounds.

+exhaustion follows BudgetExceeded semantics, not a generic CompileError.

+### 11.1 Residual Evidence And Trace Monitors
+
+The normative structured obligation/plan contract is
+[Residual Checks And Runtime Trace Monitors](etas-residual-checks-design.md).
+The execution engine owns language scope activation, ordered semantic events,
+monitor state and all exit checks. Host adapters supply typed correlated outcomes
+and trusted evidence, and continue enforcing current authority, exact sandbox
+constraints, cancellation and budgets at the real I/O boundary.
 
+An approval attempt or source-constructed result is not an accepted Host grant.
+Evidence must retain request/action/payload identity, actual outcome, issuer,
+scope and validity; unknown external completion cannot be reported as success.
+Reuse existing request/trace IDs and typed redaction/lossless-codec mechanisms.
+One semantic action may produce several Host requests, so physical request IDs
+must not be substituted for semantic action correlation.
+
+The existing `policy::TraceSpecRuntimeClient` and its label-based rule handling
+are not a complete language monitor. Remove such fallback interpretation from
+the residual enforcement path; explicit unsafe/development policy modes cannot
+prove residual coverage. A stateless PolicyClient decision may still be an
+additional deployment check, but cannot replace typed prior-evidence validity,
+scope lifecycle or exact checked event semantics. Do not move a second stateful
+language automaton into Host or CLI. A permit cannot bypass an OS resource guard.
+
+Host trace exporters are observability sinks, not the semantic monitor's input.
+Turning export off or sampling records cannot turn enforcement off. Do not infer
+permissions or approval completion by parsing formatted logs or operation names.
+
+### 11.2 Default Approval Lifetime
+
+Approval is run-scoped and in-memory by default. Bind accepted responses to the
+current root run, checked action/input and applicable narrower scope; a request
+ID/grants record alone is not proof of lifetime or transferable authority.
+Successful completion, failure or cancellation expires that run's approvals.
+Late responses cannot install grants into another run. Memory ownership and
+run identity must enforce this even when caller options/contexts are cloned.
+
+Checkpoint resume, including same-process resume, uses current authority and
+does not inherit old approvals. Preserve historical decisions/completion records
+for audit, not authorization. The engine must invalidate approval-dependent
+monitor Approved/armed readiness as well as live grants and permits. Ordinary
+await/yield, checkpoint creation in a continuing run and source-handler `resume`
+do not create a new root run. Follow the complete
+[run-scoped evidence protocol](etas-residual-checks-design.md#33-run-scoped-approval-and-explicit-reuse).
+
+Reapproval is explicit application/source/handler behavior at a safe continuation;
+neither a Host verifier nor failed restoration may automatically request approval,
+repeat external work or convert historical approval into current permission.
+An unsafe/unrepresentable continuation must be rejected before the side effect.
+
+Persistent approval reuse is disabled by default. Only application configuration
+and an injected trusted reuse provider can enable it. The provider verifies the
+issuer, accepted decision, principal, action/resource/input binding, permitted
+scope mapping, validity and applicable revocation before producing current-run
+evidence. It cannot enlarge current authority or be selected/enabled by a
+checkpoint's data. Missing/failed support fails closed, not back to old grants.
+Use the current authority/policy service layer for this optional port, with typed
+protocol values in context/authority; do not add a stateful CLI monitor or a new
+mandatory Host storage domain.
+
+Default checkpoint/resume does not require SQLite approval tables, signing keys,
+a receipt service or a generic trusted evidence store. Applications own any
+optional persistent approval backend and its retention policy. Storage write
+receipts and retained audit logs are not approval authority. No new std API or
+source syntax is introduced by this lifetime policy.
+

+
